content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and states grounds for it, which is exactly the act the rule constrains.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "The word 'ground': reading (a) the UNDERDETERMINED rests on the single verse Luke 2:48-49 being internally balanced, 'thy father' set against 'my Father's business', so that the one verse states neither the link nor its contrary; reading (b) it rests on the sufficiency of the chain answer cited ('answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4'), with the verse note being only a pointer to that answer. Since both stated clauses favor the defender, neither would produce UNDERDETERMINED unless the verse's own failure to state is doing the work, so reading (a) governs.", "why": "The judge withholds STANDS despite acknowledging the chain answer and instead rests UNDERDETERMINED on one verse's internal balance -- 'thy father' qualified by 'my Father's business' -- using the single verse's failure to state the link or its contrary as the ground, which K-S2 forbids."}
